Willie is in his final week of Shift and is excited to complete the program. His main goal is to secure employment in Greenville as he prepares to relocate to the Front Porch program, reconnect with his family, and build reliable transportation. This week, he plans to gather documents for his unclaimed property, celebrate his completion with his sisters, and spend time with family.

Willie shared that he now sees life through a healthier perspective. He feels less frustrated because he has learned to pause, examine his thoughts, manage his emotions, and update his beliefs. He believes these skills have strengthened his communication and improved his relationships with his family.

Looking ahead, Willie plans to start a business building handcrafted cedarwood model ships to sell to museums and collectors. He expressed gratitude for Turn90 and First Shift, saying the program has given him tools that will help him succeed in life.

processed_notes.note_text:
Mr. Ferguson’s primary goal upon completion of the program is to relocate back to Greenville. During case management, we discussed the two secondary goals associated with this transition: housing and employment.

Mr. Ferguson expressed a desire to remain in a sober living environment where he can continue maintaining his sobriety while also working toward long-term goals, including preparation for full retirement once he is no longer able to work. As previously noted, Mr. Ferguson currently receives $1,000 per month in SSI benefits and remains physically capable of employment despite his age.

I provided Mr. Ferguson with information regarding Front Porch Housing, a housing program in Greenville that appears well suited to his current circumstances and goals. During our session, I had him review the organization’s website and program guidelines. After reviewing the information, Mr. Ferguson stated that he was very interested in the program and did not express interest in pursuing alternative housing options at this time.

I subsequently contacted the organization and spoke with Jenna, who oversees initial applications and phone screenings. She advised that they currently have openings available and stated that she would give serious consideration to my referral, as I previously trained her in interviewing while employed there.

Given that the interview and acceptance process can take approximately 4–6 weeks, I assisted Mr. Ferguson with completing the online application during our session. Plans for next week’s case management session will focus on identifying and pursuing employment opportunities in the Greenville area.
